html:
SMTO-MAN-0008 — SMTO lost its place reading the Manual

GUID: 6aa9c70b-37f4-5666-9d9f-d4bfc0de879e
Slug: docs-invalid-cursor
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: docs

What happened

  • SMTO was reading a Manual page or list in parts, but the marker for the next part didn't match the request. The Manual itself is fine.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to open the Manual page or list again from the start. Starting over gives SMTO a new, valid marker for each next part.
  2. If it keeps happening, ask SMTO to read a smaller part, such as one section of the page. A single section often fits in one read, so no marker for a next part is needed.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the page or list without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to repeat the same request over and over; it will fail the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Manual continuation cursor failed to decode, does not match the request's reference, scope or options, or points past the end of the current document or list.

What this means

  • A continuation fails decoding/option binding, or its offset lies beyond the current document/list length. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • A continuation fails decoding/option binding, or its offset lies beyond the current document/list length.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact returned cursor, reference and retrieval options; do not edit its encoded offset.

How to fix it

  • Pass the exact next_cursor from the previous response together with the same reference (or scope, kind and tags) and include_subsections option; restart without a cursor if any option changed.
  • Use the exact next_cursor with the same reference and retrieval options.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use the exact next_cursor with the same reference and retrieval options.

How to verify the fix

  • The issued cursor works unchanged with its matching request options.

What not to do

  • Do not invent references, read arbitrary files through Docs or retry in a tight loop.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
